entry_repair_trace.first_direct_invocation: Failed before output because the direct scripts/ entry point did not add the repository root to sys.path.
entry_repair_trace.repair: Added only the conventional repository-root sys.path insertion before the uq_estimator import.

projection_and_lineage_result.finding: The observed v11.1 failure is not explained by stale files, camera-order drift, current projection-code drift, sidecar copying, or 40x40-to-10x10 target pooling. Exact reconstruction establishes implementation consistency only; it does not prove that the weak geometry target is semantically complete.

train_supervision_distribution.finding: The exact v10.1 foreground branch is strongly front-dominant. Event-balanced sampling did not make active camera views or route/actor support modes balanced.

route147_step223.diagnosis: Covered front-view pattern; useful passing contrast.

route152_step125.diagnosis: Front-left features are not strongly out of distribution, yet the frozen R prediction stays front-dominant. This is evidence of weak view/support-mode learning in addition to limited side-view coverage.

route162_step277.dominant_support: mixed; includes one actor-only rear case
route162_step277.diagnosis: The passing rear actor-only keyframe demonstrates that non-front output is possible when the representation and learned pattern are covered.

route195_step230.dominant_support: route-only; shifts from front to front-right
route195_step230.diagnosis: The two pure front-right failures have nearest-train feature cosine 0.3841 and 0.3952 with only two train events providing any front-right support. Independent-event/view coverage is a primary limitation here.

support_mode_result.finding: The held-out weakness is not only camera imbalance. Combined route-plus-actor support generalizes substantially worse than route-only support and should be reported separately in the next objective.

technical_visual_review.finding: No obvious camera-order reversal or overlay displacement was observed at contact-sheet scale. Route152 exposes coarse multi-actor rectangular support across several cameras, while Route195 exposes a route-only right-view transition. These labels remain weak supervision and require a separate semantic policy review before formal training.

next_repair_rule.name: Stage2-L R-only view-balanced support-mode-aware repair
cpu_first_requirements: Implement and unit-test a view-balanced foreground objective that gives each active camera view equal foreground-region weight within a group while preserving the calibrated soft-target optimum.
Report route-only, actor-only and combined route-plus-actor residuals separately; keep the final R output task-relevance rather than transferring task responsibility to Stage1.
Preflight the exact weight redistribution on the current 60 train groups and prove that no U, QA answer, TTC, outcome, corruption label or control field enters R.
Select additional independent train/development events with right-view support using geometry only; do not move Route152 or Route195 into train and do not read locked test outcomes.
Require nonzero accepted train coverage for every camera view intended for a formal release, including CAM_BACK_RIGHT.
next_repair_rule.first_gpu_run_after_cpu_preflight: At most one bounded R-only engineering smoke. No U-token, language, trajectory or control optimization. Preserve the existing held-out event identities and report per-view and support-mode gates.

claim_boundary: This audit proves exact reproducibility of the current weak geometry target and localizes descriptive view/support-mode/feature-coverage gaps. It does not prove that the target is semantically correct, that a view-balanced repair will generalize, that the language model uses U, that learned U is valid, or that planning is safer.
